label: executable
evidence: Goose/Core/Eval.lean; goldens first, range_loop, sampled_extent and 40+ #guard programs in Goose/Core/Examples.lean, both numeric profiles
limits: Fuel is evaluation depth plus loop iterations. Call nesting over maxCallDepth (100000) is a timeout at every fuel, so a deeply recursive terminating program has no done result. Storage is unbounded: no out-of-memory, no stack exhaustion. Store.write checks neither type nor mutability: an unchecked module can store a value of another type and run to done.
witnesses: Goldens and #guard programs in Goose/Core/Examples.lean; the pilot harness (54 fixtures agree with the compiler).

label: executable
limits: Changed while proving soundness, each in the rejecting direction: a global initializer now gets the root and effect pass and may reach only earlier globals (two accepted modules faulted: rejected_call_global_init_derefs_later, rejected_call_global_init_param_annotation); a call charges the caller with the globals the callee context lists for a parameter its summary names; a by-value loop over a run and an append count as a read of the run (rejected_summary_omits_loop_read); a summary may not name a parameter index past the parameter list (the decoder already refuses it); the root pass rechecks declaration order, which the typing pass already guarantees. The pilot harness result is unchanged (54 agree, 0 mismatch, 4 unsupported). V-MUT is not used by any proof. ValidateAgrees (Guarantees.lean) is a statement only. References to slice variables: a by-reference parameter may have type ref (slice T); its context annotation carries content roots (optional third field of vr); reads through it yield them, stores through it must lie within them, and a call requires them to denote exactly the root set of the slice variable passed, each root outliving it. No expression yields such a reference as a value, so it exists only as a parameter. The pilot harness is unchanged until the exporter emits the form; Share/Writer.lean does not write content roots, and lower emits GIR-H that gir-validate rejects (GIR-V010). After review: the contents of a let array are writable (a run sampled from a variable or global is mutable whatever its kind; assigning the variable as a whole still needs var); a writable reference or slice may initialize, rebind or be returned as a read-only one; a call of a context found never to return (its body always exits, aborts or makes such a call, with only plain statements before) ends a path; loop variables are numbered before the variables their bounds or run declare, as the tag table says. Still rejected though the compiler accepts: test/typing/return_const_recursion.goose, whose export declares a writable reference result and returns a read-only one; with the result declared read-only it validates and runs to the compiler's output. V-MUT has no semantic theorem: the evaluator has no read-only storage.

label: model-proved
statement: If Store.append o vs succeeds, every location that was readable is still readable, and every readable location that is neither the grown array nor an ancestor of it reads the same value. Typed form: if o has type grow E and the new elements have type E, every typed location stays typed, o stays grow E, the new elements are read at o++[n+i], and the store refines the old one.
differs_from_target: The target 'read (push s o v) l = read s l' is false for the grown array and its ancestors, whose content is the array, so those are excluded; the statement is about Store.append (the operation eval uses), not a separate push. Val.resizable now records its element type so that growing an empty array cannot change which array type it has.
assumptions: Typed form assumes the elements have the element type.
witnesses: sampled_extent golden: reference to element 0 read after a push; forms1 growing loop
limits: True in the model by representation: a location is a root and an element path, not an address. That the production data stacks keep elements in place is not covered.

label: model-proved
statement: validate m = ok -> for every fuel and profile, each of the fourteen evaluation functions, run on code of m from a state satisfying the frame invariant, does not fault and ends in a state satisfying it (Specs). The frame invariant contains the store invariant StoreInv: every reference or slice any root holds denotes a typed location or a run inside a typed array, and points into a root that ends no earlier than its holder. Scope exit is the block component: after execBlock releases its scope instance the frame of the surrounding code holds, because every surviving root is older than the instance and so holds no reference into it. With references to slice variables the frame also names the slice variables of callers an activation may rewrite (D) and what each may hold (A): each still holds a typed slice within A after every step, and a call restores its caller's frame from that guarantee for the variables it passed and from their being untouched for all others. The frame invariant is also where type preservation lives: every visible variable is bound to a value of its declared type at every step. Corollary in plain terms, for a run that returns: Goose.Proofs.Safety.validated_run_keeps_globals_typed (every global holds a value of its declared type).
differs_from_target: The invariant is stated over the whole store, not over a demand set (the pilot profile has no shrink, so every stored reference must stay valid). During the initialization of global g a reference to a later global may exist and be passed, but not used: the invariant there allows a reference to the whole of a global not yet bound (Unbound), and LiveRefs in the earlier sense holds once all globals are bound. The per-function statements take the validator's own results for the code as hypotheses (tyExpr = ok, rpExpr = ok); the statement free of checker functions is TH-CORE-01.
witnesses: rejected_root_forged_annotation, rejected_result_local, rejected_block_value_dangling and rejected_call_param_assumption each break the invariant at a block exit or a call and fault with dangling_root under --no-validate
limits: Grow-only pilot: the model has no shrink, so the shrink half of the target is not attempted. The invariant is established at every state a function returns in; at an abort or exit nothing is stated, since the run ends there. The earlier corollary about the final store's references was removed: a returned run's final store holds only globals, so it said nothing.

label: model-proved
theorem: Goose.Proofs.Safety.validated_context_sound; per-item facts Goose.Core.Sound.validate_modOk. Goose.Proofs.Core.validate_entry_shape is only the shape of the entry.
statement: validate m = ok -> for every context c of m, every fuel, profile and call depth, every store s satisfying StoreInv with all globals bound, and every argument list of the parameters' types whose references point into roots P gives each parameter (roots older than the call) and into the context's annotation of that parameter: enterCall does not fault, and if it returns then StoreInv holds again, every typed location is still typed, every reference stored before the call is unchanged, no root was added, and the result has the result type and points only into the roots the context declares for the result, read through P. The caller also names the slice variables it passes by reference (D) and what each may hold (A): each holds a typed slice rooted within A before and after, and each parameter that refers to one has content roots that denote exactly A of it.
differs_from_target: The target names a predicate WellFormed that is the conjunction of the validation rules as propositions. No declarative typing or root judgment was written: the checker functions remain the only statement of the rules, and what acceptance is shown to give is this semantic property of every context, stated over stores, values, locations and the module's own annotations. It is the fundamental lemma of a logical relation, not a syntactic well-formedness judgment. Its statement gained the hypotheses and the conclusion about D and A when references to slice variables were admitted; a caller that passes none takes both empty and has the earlier statement.
assumptions: validate m = ok. The hypotheses on s, the arguments and P are the precondition of the semantic property, discharged by the caller's own check at every call the evaluator makes and trivially at the entry.
witnesses: INDEX fixtures for each rule; the entry call of every golden and example module is an instance
limits: A semantic property of contexts, not the WellFormed judgment of the plan; the checker functions remain the only statement of the rules. ValidateAgrees in Guarantees.lean (acceptance iff every rule holds) is a statement only, and its attribution of fault kinds to rules is commentary.

label: model-proved
statement: validate m = ok -> forall fuel profile kind, eval fuel profile m /= fault kind, for every Module value m, about the eval and validate the tool runs.
differs_from_target: No difference in the statement. It was false of the validator this work started from: validate accepted modules that fault (see the validator row); the theorem is about the corrected validator.
assumptions: None beyond acceptance. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Goose.Core.Sound.noReturn_sound (a context found never to return yields no result) is proved separately and used for the falls-off-its-end rule.
witnesses: Non-vacuity, each a module one rule rejects that faults under --no-validate: V-TYPE rejected_type_add_bool (shape), rejected_type_global_reads_later; V-ROOT rejected_root_forged_annotation; V-BLOCK rejected_block_value_dangling; V-RESULT rejected_result_local; V-CALL rejected_call_param_assumption, rejected_call_global_init_touches_later, rejected_call_global_init_derefs_later, rejected_call_global_init_param_annotation; V-SUMMARY rejected_summary_hides_later_global (an initializer calls a function whose summary hides a read of a later global). V-MUT does not affect eval and is not used. Two checks the proof uses have no faulting witness: the root pass's recheck of declaration order never fires after the typing pass, and a summary entry for an absent parameter cannot be written in the encoding. References to slice variables: ok_captured_slice validates and runs; rejected_root_store_local_slice (V-ROOT), rejected_call_content_outlives (V-CALL) and rejected_root_forged_content (V-ROOT) each fault with dangling_root under --no-validate.
limits: core-pilot only: no shrink, construction or nonlocal return. A fault is a dangling root, a path out of range, a wrong shape at an operation, a missing table entry, a wrong argument count, or a flow leaving an expression or body; aborts, exits and timeouts are not faults. It is not type preservation (the evaluator stores any value anywhere; that variables hold values of their types is in TH-MEM-02's invariant) and it says nothing of mutability, termination, output, or exhaustion of storage or stack. Nothing composes the numeric range theorems with eval: integer values in the invariant carry their type, not their range.

The erased fields are every Context field other than impl: decl, varRoots, resultRoots. eval_eraseRoots instantiates it with a module whose contexts have no declaration key and no roots.

A different implementation index is a different program (TH-SHARE-01 covers the case where it is justified). files, types and origins are not constrained because eval reads none of them; origins are read only by the tool when it prints a line number.

label: model-proved
evidence: If Quotient m m' q rho holds then eval n p m = eval n p m' for every n and p. Quotient: header tables, entry and globals of m' equal those of m; m' has the contexts of m at the same indices with impl mapped by q; every implementation f a context of m names is, in m, the body m' holds at q f with its callees renamed by rho f; rho f sends each context to one that m' maps to the same implementation. The proof is a simulation by induction on fuel over the evaluator's mutual definitions, so mutually recursive groups need no separate argument.
limits: Differs from the target in three ways. (1) Bodies name contexts, not implementations, so the renaming that makes two bodies equal acts on context indices (rename by rho f, chosen per implementation: identity or a representative map) instead of one map q on implementation indices; q maps only the implementation index of each context. (2) Nothing is demanded of implementations no context names, which a run cannot reach; quotient_of_implwise gives the plan's every-implementation form when every context names an existing one. (3) Globals, files, types and origins must be equal (no merging of global initializers).
assumptions: None beyond the Core definitions of eval.
witnesses: test/semantics/share/INDEX (checked by run_index.sh) and Goose/Share/Examples.lean: issue-9 shape, free variable bound to two locals, mutually recursive pair, merge after one round; counterexamples: bodies differing in one operation and callees that differ stay distinct, forged merges are rejected, and the forged modules behave differently.

label: model-proved
statement: moduleOk m = true -> eval n p m = done o t -> exists k, GIR.run k p (lower m) = done o t, for every Core module m, numeric profile p, fuel n, outcome o and output t.
differs_from_target: Only the fragment moduleOk, a decidable predicate. Every global initializer and the entry function's body may use: expressions lit, bool, read, ref, slice, len, un, bin, cmp, and, or, not, conv, push, if-expressions, block expressions, array literals and fills; places var, global, deref, elem; views of and val; bounds; statements let, assign, assign-op, rebind, expression, append, if (with and without else), print, assert, abort, exit; the entry takes no parameter. It strictly contains the earlier straight-line fragment. Excluded: calls, while, for-range, for-each, return, break, continue. Nothing about faults: a Core fault is not shown to lower to a fault.
assumptions: moduleOk m = true (decidable, checked on goldens in Goose/Lower/Witness.lean). The interpreter takes the type of an integer operation from its operand, as Core does, so no typing hypothesis is needed in the fragment. The proof is by induction on Core's fuel over simulation claims for every syntactic category; the IR's fuel is existential (the claims give an equation that holds for every additional unit of fuel, so no separate fuel-monotonicity result is used). The blocks a fragment creates are handled by a builder relation (LS.Adv in Goose/Lower/Frag.lean: a fragment grows the block table, leaves every existing block but the current one unchanged, and ends in no block, its own block or a block it created) proved for every fragment of the lowering; the finished function's table extends the table at every point of the lowering (ExtT). The IR's next instruction no longer faults at a type's maximum (it adds one): the loop theorem cannot hold at every fuel otherwise, because Core's model allows an array longer than a counter type's range, and a for-range loop whose bound is such a length reaches the maximum. No fragment of this stage uses next; the change is recorded here because it alters the interpreter and the specification text for i_next ('a counter at the maximum is a fault'), which this lane does not own.
witnesses: Goldens inside moduleOk (checked with #guard in Goose/Lower/Witness.lean): gir_straight, gir_div_zero, gir_div_overflow, gir_slice_oob, gir_int_overflow_debug, gir_cast_range_debug, gir_rebind_later_same_scope, gir_assert_fail, gir_user_abort, gir_exit_code, gir_ord02 (block expression), and gir_branches, added with this stage (if with and without else, if-expression, and, or with the right operand skipped, block expression, assert, abort in one arm of an if, ending in a failed assert). test/gir/golden/mutation.sh: moving the snapshot of an indexed view after its index expression is caught by agree.

label: deferred
limits: Final third lowering attempt is parked. Concrete nonnested while statements are now proved by Goose.Lower.stmt_while_sim, and arbitrary-loop-context fragment claims plus scope-correct block initializers are checked. The module predicate and module theorem still exclude loops. Concrete range lowering needs a header invariant protecting only values before the mutable counter, because a back edge rebinds the counter below the builder value frontier; range_reentry_changes_counter proves the existing full-frontier Same invariant cannot hold, and range_reentry_keeps_prefix proves the preserved prefix. range_sim proves conditional iteration composition but its premises have not been discharged for the concrete range lowering. Nested loops, for-each, break, continue, calls and return remain unproved. A for-each over an array read through a reference additionally needs Core type safety for static owner classification. Faults are not covered.

label: model-proved
statement: validate m = ok implies, for every function: each block has exactly one terminator and it is last; every defining instruction is typed by Op.resultTy from the types of its operands and the recorded type is that type; every instruction that can abort or stands for a statement carries an origin; each implementation's summary contains the effects the provenance analysis finds. For constants, integer arithmetic, comparison, boolean negation and conversion, running on a frame whose operand cells hold the derived types finishes or aborts at an origin and never faults.
differs_from_target: Dominance and scope balance are not proved to follow from acceptance: both checks run iterative analyses (dominator sets, the scopes entered at each block) and their soundness is not argued. Typing is semantic only for the scalar operations above; memory, call and view operations are not. Reference lifetime is not implied: test/gir/invalid/gir_accepted_dangling_reference.json is accepted and its run faults with dangling_root. Summary closure is relative to the validator's own analysis.
assumptions: None beyond validate m = ok; the scalar theorem assumes the operand cells have the derived types.
witnesses: 38 modules in test/gir/invalid, each failing at the check its name gives, one accepted and faulting

label: model-proved

evidence: Goose/Lower/While.lean; added to the axiom audit; proof by induction on Core fuel.
